newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African unions should buy shares in mines - NUM.
newsitem.headline: S.African unions should buy shares in mines - NUM.

text.p: South African trade unions should buy shares in local mining houses in a bid to raise safety and living standards for workers, the National Union of Mineworkers said on Tuesday.

"Trade unions should not only negotiate wages and working conditions improvements, but should move into taking control of the mines by buying shares, in particular in small scale mines," NUM president James Motlatsi said in a statement.
Motlatsi said only a change in the structure of mine ownership would bring about real improvements in miners' conditions.

Earlier a government commissioned report said the South African mining industry, often cricitised for low pay and endemic violence, is stuck in a culture of the past that is proving too slow to change.
The report, released by the Department of Labour, is aimed at gathering information about conditions in South Africa's mining industry and making recommendations on improvements.
